summary: Three successive towers (about 1930, 1937, 1950) on Packsack Mountain; last abandoned 1967, possibly removed; no standing structure described; Weyerhaeuser permit listed for access.

facts.design: Successive towers: 10-ft enclosed platform (about 1930), 110-ft steel tower with cabin (1937), 40-ft wooden live-in tower (1950)
facts.status_note: Last tower abandoned 1967 and may have been removed; sources differ on when; no standing structure described; a 1976 survey found the old foundation

staffing.status: staffed 1952-1955 by the Bailey sisters; abandoned 1967

access.note: WillhiteWeb access note: Weyerhaeuser Pe Ell North Permit Required

events.note: Established about 1930 with a 10-foot enclosed platform tower
110-foot steel tower with accompanying cabin living quarters
40-foot wooden live-in tower built by the Washington State Division of Forestry/DNR
Bailey sisters staffed the lookout 1952 to 1955 per WillhiteWeb
Last year of the Bailey sisters' staffing per WillhiteWeb
Last tower abandoned; the register and Firelookout.com say it may have been removed around then, WillhiteWeb says a few years later
Survey crew found four 16-inch angle irons set in concrete at the old tower foundation
Registered January 19, 2012 as US 1200, WA 101; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Firelookout.com say Grays Harbor County; Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb say Pacific County. The story reports both; the record is not changed.
The register and Firelookout.com say it may have been removed around 1967; WillhiteWeb says a few years later. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: County is unresolved (Grays Harbor per FFLOS and Firelookout.com; Pacific per Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb); the story says so. The Forest Lookouts Removed status sits in a separate block after the Packsack entry, so it is quoted but not relied on for the fate. The WillhiteWeb-linked YouTube title spells the name Baily; the story follows the page's Bailey spelling.
